newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil rise on physical deals.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil rise on physical deals.

text.p: Gas oil swaps rose at midday on Wednesday following large physical purchases by a local trader which for the first time included April barrels, traders said.
"The market was spooked when the purchases went into April," one trader said.
As a result, April swaps rose sharply in fairly active morning trade to last quote at $24.95/$25.15 per barrel from Tuesday's $24.60/$24.70, brokers said.
Brokers said April traded in the morning at $24.95 and $25.00 per barrel.
March rose slightly to $26.10/$26.20 per barrel, up 10 cents from Tuesday.
Traders said the market rose because many had not expected the local trader's recent purchases to extend to April barrels as the trader had previously only bought March cargoes.
But on Tuesday, the local trader bought two 150,000-barrel cargoes at $26.65 and $26.75 per barrel, loading April 5-9 and April 6-10, respectively.
The purchases were on top of the $27.80 per barrel the trader paid for a 200,000-barrrel March 26-30 loading cargo.
Since the start of last week, the local trader had bought a total of 1.76 million barrels of gas oil.
Most players baffled by the local trader recent large purchases as regional demand does not appear to support such a large long position.
Also the first of a series of arbitrage cargoes from the West are due to hit the Asian market sometime after April 10.
Sources speculate that the raised purchases may in part be due to expectations of fresh demand from China for April cargoes.
Already stocks in Hong Kong are low with ex-terminal Hong Kong barge prices rising to about $220 per tonne, up about $10.00 from early last week.

Others worry that further hikes to Singapore swap prices may open the arbitrage again for exports from the West. Currently the April East-West stands at $21.00--a level that makes it economical for further exports of vessels are available.
Overnight, April gas oil on the International Petroleum Exchange closed down $3.75 per tonne to $165.25.
March fuel oil swaps edged up slightly to last quote at $98.00/$99.50.00 per tonne from Tuesday's $97.50/$98.50.
